---
title: "Update course material"
---

The laboratory workspace is distributed at the beginning of the course, but
new notebooks, data files, reference results or corrections may be released
later.

You do **not** need to create a new repository when this happens.

The workspace provides the command:

```bash
update-course
```

which retrieves the current instructor version of the material stored under
`course/`.

Your personal `work/` directory is not replaced by this operation.

## Before starting a newly released laboratory

Open the terminal in your existing Codespace and run:

```bash
update-course
```

Read the message printed by the command.

If the material is already current, no further update is required.

If new files have been retrieved, you may see them listed as changes in Source
Control. This is expected: they are now part of your personal repository copy
of the current course material.

## Create your personal working copy

When you start a laboratory for the first time, use:

```bash
start-lab NN
```

where `NN` is the two-digit laboratory number.

For example:

```bash
start-lab 01
```

creates the working material for Laboratory 1 under:

```text
work/lab01/
```

Open and edit the files in `work/lab01/`, not the source material under
`course/labs/lab01/`.

Running `start-lab` again does not overwrite files that already exist in your
personal working directory.

## Typical start-of-laboratory workflow

For Laboratory 2, for example:

```bash
update-course
start-lab 02
```

Then open:

```text
work/lab02/
```

and begin the activity.

::: {.callout-important}
## Protect your own work

The update mechanism is designed around the separation:

```text
course/  → distributed material
work/    → student work
```

Do not store your answers or edited notebooks inside `course/`.
:::

## If an update reports an error

Do not try to repair Git history or remove files at random.

Save your current work, synchronize it with GitHub if possible, and show the
error message to the instructor. Most update problems can be resolved without
losing anything in `work/`.
